scope: GPU Operator and NFD CPU controllers only. This is not approval of the driver/toolkit/device runtime on GPU hosts.
conditions: No Critical findings; every remaining High tuple must match this review.
GPU/NFD controller ingress is private, world egress is denied, and CPU placement excludes control-plane hosts.
Only driver operands may download packages on ports 80/443; no GPU candidate label has yet been assigned.
NFD topology updater, image-compatibility CLI, GPU sandbox/vGPU/DRA/RDMA/MIG and automatic driver upgrades are disabled.
New images, changed boundaries, changed findings or expiry require a new review.
Prometheus exporter egress is limited to GPU-system DCGM endpoints on TCP 9400; no CPU-controller public exposure is added.

high_findings.rationale: The only outbound TLS application peer is the private Kubernetes API with its mounted cluster CA; world egress is denied to both CPU controllers. No caller-supplied certificate chains or external URLs are accepted. The vulnerable verifier remains present; cluster-CA compromise or changed network exposure requires a fresh review.

The only outbound TLS application peer is the private Kubernetes API with its mounted cluster CA; world egress is denied to both CPU controllers. No caller-supplied certificate chains or external URLs are accepted. The vulnerable verifier remains present; cluster-CA compromise or changed network exposure requires a fresh review.

The controllers expose private health/metrics HTTP endpoints, not a file/range-serving API. Ingress is confined to the operator namespace and DCGM port 9400 from Prometheus. No public service is created; requests cannot select local files. The affected Go standard library is retained.

Only private HTTP health/metrics and the pinned Kubernetes API client are used. There is no public HTTP/2 listener; topology updater is disabled and CPU-controller world egress is denied. Malicious authenticated peers or an API-server compromise can still cause denial of service; bounded resources and reconciliation preserve isolation, not immunity.

No public TLS listener or submitted TLS handshakes are accepted by the configured CPU controllers. Their outbound Kubernetes API uses the cluster CA and fixed in-cluster endpoint. The affected TLS library remains installed; exposing arbitrary TLS peers invalidates this review.
